implementation.receiver_model: a 0x20-byte opaque run with NO member named anywhere in the package, and every access made through a displacement-named accessor: word_at(self, kReceiverGateWordDisplacement) for the dword at +0x1c (0x00641fa3), word_at(self, kReceiverTableDisplacement) for the word at +0x00 (0x00641fb9) and address_at(self, kReceiverSubObjectDisplacement) for the +0x04 region the LEA at 0x00641fa9 forms without loading it. implementation.dispatch_model: one indirect transfer, TWO-LEVEL and both levels fixed by this body's own listing: the table pointer is the dword at the receiver's +0x00 (0x00641fb9 MOV EDX,[ESI]) and the slot word is the dword at table+0x68, index 26 (0x00641fbb MOV EAX,[EDX+0x68]), called through the register at 0x00641fc0 CALL EAX with ECX = the receiver and no stack word. mechanics.body_shape: A three-input conjunction with one shared false exit. 0x00641fa3..0x00641fc4 is a straight-line chain of three tests and all three JZ targets are the SAME instruction, 0x00641fca. There is no other branch in the body, so the whole control flow is: test the receiver's word at +0x1c against zero; if zero return 0; call 0x00641900 with the address of receiver+0x04; if its AL is zero return 0; load the receiver's own +0x00 as a table pointer and its +0x68 as a slot; call that slot with the receiver in ECX; if its AL is zero return 0; otherwise return the constant 1. All three exits converge on either MOV AL,0x1 / POP ESI / RET or XOR AL,AL / POP ESI / RET.
mechanics.receiver_displacement: Three, all from this body's own listing, and all of the body's receiver traffic: 0x00 loaded at 0x00641fb9 (the dispatch table pointer); 0x04 addressed at 0x00641fa9 (LEA, so no load, and the dword stored there is never tested here); 0x1c loaded at 0x00641fa3 (CMP against zero). The machine-derived receiver record enumerates offsets [0, 28] -- that is 0x00 and 0x1c, the two it can see -- and carries bounds_only, so it states where the body was seen reaching and not which member is which. Nothing else on the receiver is read or written: the modeled type is a 0x20-byte opaque run, which is exactly 0x1c + 4, the last byte the body's only receiver load touches.
mechanics.layout_derivation: The 0x0c sub-object at receiver+0x04 is NOT shown by this body, which only takes its address. Its two-word layout comes from the one direct callee's own 88-instruction listing, read for this package: 0x0064192e MOV ECX,[EAX] and 0x00641930 MOV EDX,[EAX+8] with EAX loaded from the callee's argument at 0x0064192a. The run between the two words is touched by nothing in this set and is declared as an opaque four-byte pad. The dispatch table's layout is not derived at all: this body reads one word out of it, the package gives the table no type and no members, and the 30-slot extent that exists purely so the slot index is measurable lives in the model test's own fixture rather than in the model. Nothing is claimed about the other 29 slots.
mechanics.control_flow: 22 instructions, one straight-line chain, three conditional branches, all of them JZ to the same address 0x00641fca, plus two unconditional returns. No loop, no switch, no computed jump. There is no instruction whose meaning depends on a path being taken more than once, so the body is straight-line and the model needs no iteration.
mechanics.branch_polarity: Every one of the three is a JZ, i.e. the branch is TAKEN when the tested value is zero. So all three gates are true when their value is NONZERO. The two callee gates are the two-byte TEST AL,AL idiom (0x00641fb5 and 0x00641fc2), which tests the whole of AL against zero: zero is false and every other byte 0x01..0xff is true. They are emphatically not comparisons against 1, and the model test drives 0x02, 0x37, 0x80, 0xfe and 0xff through both of them.
mechanics.not_modelled: The body contains no store instruction, so no memory effect, cache, refcount or flag write is modelled and none is claimed. The three return statements in the model are the same 0x00641fca path the JZs name, written as early returns because the shared exit is spelled once per arm; they are not three exits. The saved ESI is a machine fact recorded in observed_original_abi and not reproduced in the model -- see validation.not_verified for why the model test does not assert it.
mechanics.globals: none. No instruction in the 22 names a data-segment address, and the machine-derived globals list for this VA is empty.

mechanics.return_semantics_machine: AL is written explicitly on all three paths and nowhere else: MOV AL,0x1 at 0x00641fc6 on the satisfied path, XOR AL,0x1's counterpart XOR AL,AL at 0x00641fca on the shared false exit. So the observable result is the CONSTANT 1 or the CONSTANT 0 and the dispatch target's own byte is never propagated -- a target returning 0x37 still yields exactly 1. The declared type is therefore a byte, not a bool, and not the callee's return type: only AL is ever written, so the upper three bytes of EAX are the dispatch target's leftovers and no record fixes them. The record's own abi.return_semantics is 'integral_in_EAX' with return_register EAX, which is consistent and does not pin the width; the width is pinned by MOV AL rather than MOV EAX.
mechanics.receiver_writes: none. There is no store instruction in the 22. The model test byte-compares the whole receiver (0x90 bytes, i.e. the 0x20 the model claims plus a decoy field past it) and the whole table before and after every call, so 'this body writes nothing, and writes nothing past its modeled extent either' is asserted rather than assumed.

return_semantics.value: exactly 0 or exactly 1. 1 iff the receiver's dword at +0x1c is nonzero AND 0x00641900's AL is nonzero AND the byte the slot at table+0x68 returns is nonzero; 0 otherwise. The value returned by the dispatch target is tested for nonzero and then discarded.
return_semantics.ownership: The body acquires and releases nothing. It reads two dwords of the receiver, forms one address, reads one dword through a table pointer the receiver supplied, and calls through it. Whether the receiver owns the table, borrows it or holds it by smart handle is not established by any record for this target and is not claimed.
return_semantics.lifetime: There is no frame object: the body reserves no stack space and stores nothing of its own. The only address it creates is receiver+0x04, which is borrowed for the duration of the 0x00641900 call and outlives it; what that callee does with it, and whether anything it hands back survives, is 0x00641900's business and is not modelled here.

Its `(**(code **)(*param_1 + 0x68))()` does reproduce the two-level dispatch and the 0x68 displacement, and it calls the slot with no arguments, which agrees with the listing. unresolved_questions: What the dword at receiver+0x1c IS. The body compares it against zero and never dereferences it, so it is a null-ness gate on a word whose type, ownership and producer no record for this VA establishes. It is modelled as an opaque Word and nothing more. Naming it (a handle, a flag word, a version) would be a member story the listing does not carry.

What the 0x0c sub-object at receiver+0x04 is, and what 0x00641900 decides. This package fixes only that the callee is handed its address, reads the dwords at +0x00 and +0x08 through it, and returns a byte. 0x00641900's own body is 88 instructions long, has one direct call of its own (0x0067dcd0) and two levels of virtual dispatch, and is not this worker's target; it is unowned here.

Which concrete function the slot at table+0x68 holds. It is a per-vtable choice: 0x00b1fbf0 in the table at 0x01462764, 0x006418b0 in the table at 0x01489090. The slot's own signature is taken from the CALL SITE (receiver in ECX, no stack word, byte in AL) and nothing fixes what the implementations do or whether they agree with each other.

Whether a live receiver is ever dispatched through the four-slot table at 0x013ff6ac, in which this body is index 3. If it is, the index-0x68 word this body loads is data past that table rather than one of its slots. The two larger tables show real content at index 26, so the two-level load is not in doubt; what is open is which table a given receiver carries.

Whether the class name Sporepedia::cSPAssetDataOTDB applies to THIS virtual. It applies to the eight neighbours that share the vtable family and to the family as a whole, but this body is one of seven xref'd slots in seven different tables and a virtual's declaring class is fixed by the table it is called through, which is not established here. The type name in the header is labelled INFERRED for that reason.

The semantic name of the predicate. The shape -- three inputs, one direct callee, one virtual slot, a null-ness gate -- is fully reconstructed, but nothing in the evidence says what question the boolean answers. 'IsEditable' is the name the repository gives the neighbour at 0x00641400 and the shapes differ; it is deliberately NOT borrowed here.

Whether the machine's own return classification should ever be spelled as a type, and the answer for this VA is NO. The record's register-class phrase is 'byte boolean, normalised to {0, 1}' (kept verbatim in observed_original_abi.return_type_machine_classification and as return_semantics.kind). That is a CLASSIFICATION of the value the machine leaves in EAX -- it says which bytes are written and what the value set is -- and it is not a C or C++ type: no declaration can be spelled to match it, which is why it sat in return_type and produced a permanent 'return type differs or is semantically renamed' against a span that was correct. It is now recorded in its own field instead. THE CAUSE is a fact about the two compilers, not about the 22-instruction listing and not about this package's source. On x86-32 clang never materialises a `push` for a cdecl call argument: it stores the argument into the outgoing-argument area at the CURRENT %esp and calls. At -O0 the disassembly of this package's own reconstruction (clang++ -std=c++17 -m32 -c) reads `sub $0x44,%esp` in the prologue, then at the call site `mov %eax,(%esp)` / `call`, and the indirect dispatch at 0x00641fc0's model site is `call *%eax` with %esp unchanged between them, so BOTH callees are entered at the SAME %esp and the measured gap is 0. The same happens at -O1 and at -O2 (verified: `lea 0x4(%ecx),%eax` / `mov %eax,(%esp)` / `call`), so this is a compiler-family difference and not an unoptimised-build artifact. GCC, by contrast, emits a real `pushl` plus `sub $0xc,%esp` of alignment padding, which is what the test's own comment on N4 already describes; under g++ the gap is 16 and N2/N3/N4 all hold. The test's N4 comment already concedes that 'the absolute gap is NOT asserted to be exactly four, and the reason is a fact about the compiler rather than about the listing' -- N2 and N3 turn out to be in that same family, one step stronger.
